chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you think of a vessel of intoxicant upon which water is poured until its strength disappears and its intoxication goes away? He said: 'By God, not a single drop that drips from it in a jug will be poured out, but that jug will be poured out (discarded).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water poured over an intoxicant to remove its strength?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *kathrah* (abundance) in impurities, ruling that pouring water over an intoxicant to remove its essence does not purify the mixture. He emphasizes that the entire vessel's content remains impure, using the metaphor of a jug (*hubb*) to illustrate that even a single drop taken from it carries the impurity, thereby rejecting the notion that dilution alone renders the substance halal. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between mere removal of taste and actual purification of the substance.
